title: Drinking on the bandstand and the oil-field setting at the Ramona
summary: Musicians bought their own drinks except a free fifth from the owner at 11 o'clock; Watts says he sipped carefully, and describes the oil-field smell.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Yeah, nobody give you no drink, they don't pass nothing. Now he ain't gonna drink that fast. When he feels tired, he sips it, you see? And I done very well there for a year, I never did get drunk, because I did just like the old piano player, it hasn't been there a long time, you just sip. And that picks you up when you get tired, see? You understand? See?

Now you can make a little high ball, because I never did like it straight, because whiskey always was strong in my throat, you know? I'd get a little something, you know, Coke or 7-Up and make, but I have a fifth too. Now you didn't have to do nothing. When you get at 11 o'clock at night, that was your free. You just throw your finger up. And Cesar Thompson from your bandstand, the big ballroom here and your big long horseshoe ball over there, he'd look up there about that time, he'd look at his time up over the ball, and he'd look at you, and you'd do that. Well now he'd send you a fifth, see? Now that's for the seven men, see? See, you go ahead and see Thomas, he cut his band a lot to play this job, see? I mean they didn't, he had 10 pieces in San Anzo, but they didn't all make the scene on this job in the harp, see, because they didn't like the idea of it, see, of going to the harp, you see? Because they said they had, Thomas said he had been there one time and you could smell harp by 20 miles before you got to it, and they never did think they could get used to that old oil smell, you know. You don't think you could sit on it, but man, you get used to it so fast, man, it's a shame. Shucks, you don't smell them things, and in the people's front yard where it's supposed to be grass, man, you see them big arms that are all pumping day and night. Yeah. Well anyway, we, I worked there all about a year with Tommy Brooks, and then a band was working over at the Tokyo Club, that's another jitney. Right, that was right across, oh I'd say about six or seven blocks from the Ramona, across. Nothing, hardwood and built stuff like it is now, I reckon, I wouldn't know it, I haven't been back so long. Oh yeah. But there's nothing but mesquite bushes and desert, till you get to the other club. That's 40 years ago.
